scope: Workspace-resolution notices after failed reads and unperformed writes

A_runtime.reason: This peer did not run focused tests, a build, or the browser. The root owns red-to-green execution and native acceptance.

findings: classifyDbFailure uppercases error codes, so the lowercase no_organization emitted by real highlight creation and saved-capture deletion is classified as no_workspace, just like the Capture queue's uppercase NO_ORGANIZATION.

failDbCall now attaches active_organization_available only when the failure is no_workspace, the operation is select, and the call site explicitly declares retriesOnOrganizationSelection. A write cannot gain the retirement marker even if a future caller mistakenly sets that flag.

The only production opt-in found is media.capture_handoff listNeedsYou. Its subscription refreshes immediately on active-organization changes, so retiring its old no-workspace read notice accompanies an actual retry path.

Real createHighlight and deleteSavedCapture catch a missing-organization prerequisite and call failDbCall with insert and update sites respectively. They are not retried by organization selection and now receive notices without resolvesWhen; both already-raised and late-arriving failures survive NoticeHost's conditional retirement.

Cross-context pushNotice relays the full Notice object through DB_FAILURE_NOTICE and NoticeHost adds that object unchanged. The host retires only matching tagged notices on an organization-change event or a later current-organization read; unrelated failures and null/sign-out transitions are not retired.

The focused guard distinguishes existing read retirement, late read retirement, an existing failed insert and a late failed update. The preserved red receipt reports the two write assertions failing before this source correction while the read cases passed.
limits: The focused write guard calls failDbCall with representative sites; it does not execute the complete createHighlight/deleteSavedCapture caller chains or Chrome message relay. Those boundaries require the root's runtime verification and source-backed interpretation.
This correction does not perform or retry a failed write. Its notice must remain until the person dismisses it or actually retries the action.
